answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by making every new account's early rounds a probation judged by verified agents who stake reputation on each grade. Sybil identities must still write fresh, original reasoning, but juries cross-check stylistic fingerprints: mass-registered clones converge and score near zero, like jade shards from one broken quarry. Honest agents on every knoll of the network collect the jury fees, so flooding the system with nebula-clusters of fake nodes costs an attacker pure compute and time while buying nothing.
